papers.title: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties
papers.version: Published 6 April 2018; main publisher PDF hosted by author lab
papers.summary: Learned crystal graphs predict properties and expose site-level design patterns.

representation.rationale: Learned relations enrich a supplied crystal-graph vocabulary.

transfer.rationale: Graph learning transfers into crystal-property prediction.

formal.rationale: Pooling enforces permutation and unit-cell-size invariance.

organization.rationale: Training and prediction follow a fixed workflow.

explanation.rationale: Site contributions reveal quantified chemical preferences.

validation.rationale: Held-out calculations test a surrogate, without new synthesis.

robustness.rationale: Architecture comparisons and new crystals; distribution-shift limits remain.

surprise.observation: An interpretable pooling constraint exposes promising perovskite site preferences.
surprise.interpretation: Standard prediction research can generate design insight.
surprise.boundary: Learned site energies are model contributions, not separately measured atomic energies.

detail.observation: Interpretable pooling worsens perovskite MAE from 0.099 to 0.130 eV/atom.
detail.consequence: Interpretability and predictive accuracy are different objectives.

read: Main six-page published PDF, including equations, comparisons and perovskite case
notRead: Raw data, code execution or independent reproduction

papers.title: E(3)-equivariant graph neural networks for data-efficient and accurate interatomic potentials
papers.summary: Equivariant tensor features enable data-efficient forces and molecular dynamics.

representation.rationale: Tensor features enrich a fixed atomistic representation.

transfer.rationale: Geometric learning is applied within atomistic prediction.

formal.rationale: Composed equivariant layers and energy-gradient forces enforce symmetry and conservation.

dynamics.rationale: Simulations target structural and kinetic response.

organization.rationale: Learning and evaluation use a fixed pipeline.

explanation.rationale: Controlled tensor-order comparisons isolate an architectural explanation.

validation.rationale: Direct MD tests structure and diffusion against AIMD.

robustness.rationale: Ablations, data budgets and phase tests; extrapolation remains bounded.

surprise.observation: Equivariance changes learning-curve slopes in tested systems.
surprise.interpretation: Formal inductive bias can change data efficiency, beyond shifting accuracy.
surprise.boundary: This is an empirical architecture effect, not universal learning theory.

detail.observation: Many benchmark splits sample frames from shared trajectories; glass tests also cross melt-to-quench.
detail.consequence: Held-out-frame accuracy and phase transfer provide distinct evidence.

read: Publisher main HTML: architecture, equivariance, results, data efficiency and Methods
Software versions, split construction and learning-curve controls

papers.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials
papers.status: Peer-reviewed Nature article; author correction in January 2026
papers.version: Corrected publisher HTML accessed 15 October 2026; title and counts reflect correction
papers.summary: Literature, thermodynamics, active learning and robotics close a synthesis loop.

representation.rationale: Recipes evolve within supplied phase and synthesis representations.

transfer.rationale: Knowledge and algorithms combine within inorganic synthesis.

formal.rationale: Interfaces and constraints organize a modular pipeline.

dynamics.rationale: Reaction outcomes serve synthesis endpoints, not designed dynamical functions.

organization.rationale: Recipe adaptation occurs within prescribed workflow and targets.

explanation.rationale: Failure analysis identifies actionable synthesis barriers.

validation.rationale: Robotics performs synthesis and XRD characterization.

robustness.rationale: Manual phase rechecks support outcomes; pipeline-level alternatives remain open.

surprise.observation: Physical autonomy already exists outside Buehler’s agent frameworks.
surprise.interpretation: Self-organization must be distinguished from autonomous execution.
surprise.boundary: This is a strong chosen comparator, not a typical-field percentile.

detail.observation: Corrected record reports 36 of 57 targets, with four further XRD-inconclusive cases.
detail.consequence: Use corrected evidence, and distinguish new-to-algorithm from globally novel materials.
detail.locator: Experimental synthesis outcomes; Methods: Materials screening; 2026 correction
